_ko.title: POV: 앱으로 한국어를 배웠는데… 바리스타가 밥 먹자고 한다?! 🍚
_ko.description:
「다음에 밥 한번 먹어요!」 — 교과서 머리로는 저녁 초대! 📅
실제로는 대개 「또 봐요」 같은 다정한 인사야. 날짜를 안 잡아도 돼. 😅

이 말을 들으면 이렇게만 해:
👉 네, 좋아요! — 좋아요!
(친구끼리는 반말로 「다음에 밥 한번 먹자!」)
(정말 만나고 싶으면 상대가 먼저 날짜를 물어 올 거야 😉)

또 아는 한국어 「예의상 하는 말」은? 👇

en.title: POV: you learned Korean from an app… and the barista asks you to dinner?! 🍚 #learnkorean
en.description:
“다음에 밥 한번 먹어요!” (Let's grab a meal sometime!) — your textbook brain says: a dinner invite! 📅
In real life it's usually just a friendly goodbye, like “see you around.” No date needed. 😅

When you hear it, just say:
👉 네, 좋아요! — Sounds good!
(Between friends you'll hear the casual version: 다음에 밥 한번 먹자!)
(If they really mean it, they'll ask you for a date. 😉)

What other Korean “polite lies” do you know? 👇

en.alt: A needle-felted café. A small coral ghost-shaped plush stands on the counter next to an iced americano while a felt barista waves goodbye and says “다음에 밥 한번 먹어요!” (Let's grab a meal sometime!). The plush lights up, opens a felt calendar on its phone and asks “와! 언제요? 화요일 7시?” (Wow! When? Tuesday at 7?). The barista's wave freezes with an awkward smile — “아, 네. 그냥, 다음에요.” (Uh… yeah. Just… sometime.) — under a NOT A REAL PLAN stamp. A paused-café card titled REAL KOREAN THAT WORKS explains: 다음에 밥 한번 먹어요 is not a real plan, it means “See you around!”; when you hear it, just say 네, 좋아요! (Sounds good!), with a pause to say it out loud. The plush says it, the barista happily waves “네! 또 오세요!” (Great! Come again!), and the video asks what other Korean “polite lies” you know.
